preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 100000 and 1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 100000 and line.split()[0] != line.split()[1] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: All edges have distinct vertices u_i and v_i within bounds 1..n, and no self-loops or multiple edges exist.

preconditions.expression: all(line.split()[2] in {'B', 'R'} for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each edge's color is either 'B' (blue) or 'R' (red).

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == m + 1 and all(line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines())
preconditions.description: Input has exactly m+1 lines (n, m on first line, followed by m edges), with no empty lines.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (stdout.strip().split() and int(stdout.strip().split()[0]) >= 0 and all(1 <= int(v) <= n for v in stdout.strip().split()[1:]))
postconditions.description: Output is either '-1' (no solution) or a non-negative integer k followed by k vertex indices in 1..n.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (lambda: any(all((u in selected_vertices or v in selected_vertices) % 2 == (initial_color != target_color) for u, v, initial_color in edges) for selected_vertices in [set(stdout.strip().split()[1:])] for target_color in ['B', 'R']))()
postconditions.description: If output is not '-1', there exists a target color (all 'B' or all 'R') such that toggling vertices in the output set flips each edge's color to the target color. The output set is minimal in size.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == '-1' or (lambda: not any(all((u in selected_vertices or v in selected_vertices) % 2 == (initial_color != target_color) for u, v, initial_color in edges) for selected_vertices in [set(v) for v in combinations(range(1, n+1), k)] for target_color in ['B', 'R'] if len(v) < k))() if (k := int(stdout.strip().split()[0])) > 0 else True
postconditions.description: If output is not '-1', the number of moves k is minimal (no smaller set of vertices achieves the goal).
